Relationship safety

Domestic Violence, Relationship Safety & Support

Abuse can include physical violence, threats, sexual coercion, stalking, isolation, financial control, intimidation, technology abuse, or other patterns used to control another person.

Last updated September 19, 2026 · Editorial policy

If you are in immediate danger:

Call 911 or move to a safer location if you can do so safely. Be mindful that phones, browsing history, location services, and shared accounts may be monitored.

Safety planning can be individualized

A domestic-violence advocate can help someone think through housing, children, transportation, documents, finances, digital privacy, pets, legal options, and emergency contacts without requiring the person to make a specific decision about the relationship.

National support

The National Domestic Violence Hotline has historically provided phone, chat, and text support in the U.S. Before public launch, this page should be checked against the hotline's current official contact information and linked directly to the verified source.

Treasure Valley resources

We will add verified shelters, advocacy programs, victim services, and legal-assistance options after a live-source review.

Need urgent help?

If there is immediate danger or a medical emergency, call 911. In the U.S., call or text 988 for the Suicide & Crisis Lifeline.
